transcript: Last night, I saw The Great Gatsby on Broadway. Now, I had heard extremely mixed things about this production, and it's getting a lot of buzz, and maybe this is a boring take, but I feel pretty neutral about it. I think it really delivers on what you'd expect it to like the glitzy 1920s aesthetic and obviously the vocals from Jeremy Jordan and Eva Noblezada. But there are a couple of caveats here. Although the big production numbers are super fun and make great use of the stage, there are other scenes with just one or two actors performing a scene or song on what feels like a massive, empty stage. And these are the kinds of scenes where the vocals really get to shine, but the music in my opinion didn't hit quite the way I would have hoped. Don’t get me wrong, the music was very pleasing to the ear and really well performed but it just wasn't really that memorable to me. And I think the plot and the characters inherently aren't that interesting to me, so I was kind of hoping the score might do some lifting in that regard. Also when you have vocalists like Jeremy Jordan and Eva Noblezada I imagine it's very difficult to find a score that can really match what they're bringing to the table. So overall I thought this was a fine production that did a lot of things right, and in a lot of regards is quite enjoyable, but I just wasn't very invested. And I think The Great Gatsby is just a really hard story to adapt for the stage, and maybe it's just not my cup of tea. With that, another playbill for my collection.
